amplitude_level.doc:
The amplitude and offset of a 1 Vpp waveform, as the instrument defines them (D13, D48).

``amplitude`` is in ``unit``: VPP, VPK, VRMS (through each function's peak-to-RMS ratio: sine
2√2, square and pulse 2, ramp 2√3 Vpp per Vrms) or DBM (the power into the load setting:
Vrms = √(10^(dBm/10) · 1 mW · R)). The level is what a load of ``load_setting`` ohms would see
behind ``output``'s impedance, so the EMF is raised by (R + Z) / R; ``inf``, or ``hiz_from`` ohms
and more, is high-Z: the level is the open-circuit voltage and dBm is referred to
``dbm_hiz_ohms`` (50 Ω, the usual convention when the load is unknown).

``vpp_min`` / ``vpp_max`` bound the amplitude as volts peak-to-peak into the load setting, the
one physical limit a source has (D48): a write in any unit is converted and checked, refusing
with -222; a change of the waveform or the load setting that would leave the range is refused
with -221. Switching the unit converts the value, so the output does not move (a real source's
``VOLT:UNIT``); there is no dBm expression of 0 Vpp, so that switch is refused with -221.

params.doc: in unit

params.doc: VPP | VPK | VRMS | DBM

arb_table.doc:
An arbitrary waveform: a table played at ``rate`` samples per second, linearly interpolated.

The output is periodic with fundamental ``rate / N``. Linear interpolation between samples is a
convolution with a triangle, so harmonic k carries ``X[k mod N] / N · sinc²(k / N)``: the
spectrum is exact, not sampled (validation-lockin.md 6). Harmonics are kept up to ``max_lines``.

calibration_store.doc:
Calibration coefficients keyed by the measurement context, and the calibration ledger.

A measuring core references the store with ``store: <this component's name>`` and reads its
reading as ``(raw − offset[key]) × gain[key]``; a key never adjusted gives gain 1 and offset 0.
The key comes from the ``key`` parameter, one entry per key dimension:

* ``$path`` - the value of that instrument state (e.g. ``$sense.function``);
* ``component.param`` - that component's parameter; for the calibrated core itself,
  ``function`` is the function of the measurement being made and ``range`` the range actually
  in use (the auto-chosen one included), e.g. ``[meter.function, meter.range]``.

``adjust`` (a reference of 0 adjusts the zero, anything else the gain) checks the core's raw
input against the reference first: the deviation must stay within ``tolerance`` of the
reference (of ``max(|reference|, 1)`` for the zero, where the reference itself is 0). A failed
check pushes the calibration error (702 by default) and replies ``fail_reply``. Adjusted
coefficients take effect at once and become permanent when ``store`` commits them; whether an
un-stored adjustment survives ``*RST`` is ``volatile_until_store``. The ledger (``count``,
``date``, ``time``, ``string``) and the security ``code`` are never touched by ``*RST``.
``secured`` and ``value`` may be bound to instrument state (``$cal.secured``); set through the
ops they write that state back, so the store follows the instrument's own variables.

params.name: secured
params.doc: calibration secured: adjusting needs the security code

params.name: code
params.doc: the factory security code

params.name: key
params.doc: key dimensions: '$state.path' or 'component.param' entries

params.name: value
params.doc: the reference a gain adjustment assumes on the input (a setting)

params.name: tolerance
params.doc: fraction of the reference the input may be off by

params.name: ok_reply
params.doc: reply of a successful adjustment

params.name: fail_reply
params.doc: reply of a failed adjustment

params.name: volatile_until_store
params.doc: *RST drops adjustments that were not stored

operations.name: adjust
operations.doc: Adjust for the current key: a reference of 0 zeroes, any other adjusts the gain.

operations.name: code
operations.doc: A new security code; the calibration must be unsecured.

operations.doc: How many calibrations have been stored (a query; the count is not settable).

operations.name: date
operations.doc: The date of the last stored calibration (a query).

operations.name: secure
operations.doc: :CALibration:SECure:STATe {ON|OFF},<code>: unsecuring needs the security code.

operations.name: store
operations.doc: :CALibration:STORe - keep the adjustments; counts the calibration and dates it.

operations.name: string
operations.doc: The calibration message; written by the user, survives *RST.

operations.name: time
operations.doc: The time of the last stored calibration (a query).

operations.name: value
operations.doc: The reference a gain adjustment assumes on the input.

calibrator_control.doc:
The calibrator's output control (#329): ``operate`` (standby disconnects the terminal),
``z_out``, ``i_max`` (the overload trip back to standby with ``overload_error``) and
``standby_above`` (a change of the output to or from above it returns to standby). It drives
the setpoint block's signal onto the electrical terminal.

params.doc: False: standby, the terminal is disconnected

params.name: z_out
params.doc: ohm, output impedance (0: an ideal source)

params.name: i_max
params.doc: A, beyond this load current the output trips to standby (<= 0: never)

``OPER`` (value true) or ``STBY`` (false): enter or leave operate; entering starts the
settling of the level.

calibrator_output.doc:
A calibrator's setpoint and output control in one block: ``function`` (DCV | ACV),
``level`` (V; RMS for ACV), ``frequency`` (Hz; 0 for DCV), ``operate``, ``z_out``, ``i_max``,
``settle`` (s, or a table per function), ``standby_above`` (V), and the hidden
``gain_error_ppm`` / ``offset`` of the output stage. The same behaviour as
``calibrator_setpoint`` + ``calibrator_control`` (#329), for definitions written before the
split.

The settings are bound to instrument state (``function: $out.function`` ...); the commands
write the state and the component follows. ``settle`` is taken from the table by the target
function when it is a dict (``{DCV: 1.0, ACV: 2.0}``).

The calibrator's setpoint and range generation (#329): ``function`` (DCV | ACV), ``level``

coax_cable.label: 同轴线缆
coax_cable.doc:
A short cable: a small series resistance (no delay or reflections).

``r_skin_1mhz`` adds the skin effect: a series impedance ``r_skin_1mhz * sqrt(f / 1 MHz) * (1 + j)``
(resistance and internal reactance rise together with the square root of frequency), which
makes a 50 Ω path lose a little more at higher frequencies and a square wave settle slowly
after each edge. A lumped model, valid while the cable is short against the wavelength.

params.name: r
params.doc: series resistance

params.name: length_m
params.doc: cable length (no delay is modeled)

params.name: r_skin_1mhz
params.doc: skin impedance at 1 MHz, rising as the square root of frequency

counter_core.doc:
The counting core (F #192): frequency, period, totalize and time interval over the gate.

Frequency and period use reciprocal counting over the events inside the gate, so a fast
timebase reads low by ε (the same convention as the spectrum analyzer's display); totalize
reports the crossings inside the gate; time interval is measured between the first event on
channel A and the next on channel B, plus each channel's trigger error (normal, seeded by the
virtual instant, so two readings at one instant agree).

params.name: function
params.doc: FREQuency | PERiod | TOTalize | TINTerval | TSTamp (time stamps, #385)

params.name: gate
params.doc: the counter_gate

params.name: clock
params.doc: the reference_clock (timebase)

params.name: a_input
params.doc: the counter_input of channel A (threshold, sensitivity)

params.name: b_input
params.doc: the counter_input of channel B

params.name: statistics
params.doc: the counter_statistics (empty: no statistics)

params.name: single_shot_s
params.doc: s, the interpolator's single-shot resolution (model value)

params.doc: Hz, the highest rate time stamps are generated at (TSTamp:RATE, #385)

operations.doc: ``:MEASure:<function>?``: one gated measurement, taking the gate time.

operations.name: timestamps
operations.doc: The timebase's timestamps (s) of the next ``count`` rising edges on channel A (#328).

counter_gate.doc:
The gate (F #192): its time and source, and the true duration the timebase produces. A fast
timebase makes the instrument's second short, so the gate lasts ``T / (1 + ε)`` of true time.

params.name: time
params.doc: s, the gate time

params.name: source
params.doc: INTernal | EXTernal (who starts the gate: the trigger model)

params.name: clock
params.doc: the reference_clock the gate time is counted on

counter_input.doc:
One input channel (F #192): impedance (1 MΩ or 50 Ω) at the pin, AC/DC coupling, the trigger
level and the sensitivity (the smallest peak-to-peak amplitude the channel counts; below it the
signal is rejected as noise).

params.name: z_in
params.doc: input resistance to ground, ohm (the 1 MΩ / 50 Ω setting)

params.name: coupling
params.doc: DC | AC input coupling

params.name: ac_corner

counter_statistics.doc:
The statistics block (F #192): the measurements taken, and their mean, minimum, maximum and
standard deviation (sample standard deviation, n − 1).

params.doc: measurements kept (the oldest go past this)

counter_timebase.doc:
The counter's timebase (#328, component-map frequency_counter.timebase): the reference clock
turned into the instrument's time scale. A timestamp is the true instant on that scale — a fast
clock reads time long by its error ε — with the interpolator's single-shot resolution (normal,
seeded by the instant, so a repeated reading agrees).

``gap_free`` is continuous measurement without dead time: each frequency reading spans from the
previous gate's last edge to this gate's last edge, so adjacent readings share their boundary
edge and the readings times their spans add up exactly to the edges counted (the 53230A's
gap-free mode; without it each gate measures its own first-to-last edge span).

params.name: clock
params.doc: the reference_clock the timebase runs on

params.name: single_shot_s
params.doc: s, the interpolator's single-shot resolution (rms)

params.name: gap_free
params.doc: continuous gates without dead time (a setting)

Traces sampled at a rate into bins, with start, pause, resume and reset (#273).

The SR830's data storage: two traces (the CH1/CH2 displays), 62.5 mHz – 512 Hz or one point
per trigger, single shot or loop, ``TRCA?``/``TRCB?``/``TRCL?`` reading k points from bin j.

value followed by a comma; ``FLOAT``: IEEE single precision, little-endian; ``LIA``: the
SR830's 16-bit mantissa/exponent pairs.

``CAPTUREVAL? n``: every recorded trace's value at bin ``n`` (0: the oldest), comma
separated; a bin inside the buffer that holds no data yet reads 0 (the zero fill).

Start (or resume) the scan; ``fresh`` discards what is stored first (the SR86x's
CAPTURESTART clears the buffer and starts a new capture).

dmm_adc.doc:
The A/D (#190 E1): digits, NPLC reading time, resolution, calibration and the reading.

It reads the conditioning block's raw value, applies the calibration coefficients and the
resolution quantization, and turns a reading beyond ``overrange`` × full scale into
``overload_value``. Calibration: with ``store`` naming a ``calibration_store`` component the
reading is corrected with the store's per-key coefficients (metrology-authoring.md 4) and the
``cal_*`` operations delegate to it; without a store the single legacy coefficient set below
applies. The component is the instrument's sampler (metrology-authoring.md 3.1).

params.doc: display digits of a reading

params.doc: a reading beyond this fraction of full scale is an overload

params.doc: the reading an overload produces

params.doc: legacy (no store): calibration zero (offset) coefficient

params.doc: legacy (no store): calibration security code

operations.doc: :CALibration:ZERO? — with 0 V applied, make the reading zero. Replies 0 (done) or 1 (failed).

operations.name: configure
operations.doc:
CONFigure?'s range and resolution: the effective range, and the resolution step in use.

The resolution is the one CONFigure was given (``set_resolution``, #286: the manual says
the argument specifies the measurement resolution and CONFigure? reports it); when it is
unset the step comes from the ``resolution`` mapping of the integration time, as before.
The readings themselves quantize by ``resolution`` either way — the model boundary is
noted in the definition's coverage table.

operations.name: range
operations.doc: The range in use, the auto-chosen one included (the definition's range query).

dmm_conditioning.doc:
Signal conditioning (#190 E1): function, ranges and the AC filter, and the analog errors.

DC (mean) and true-rms AC of the signal on its input; AC is the rms of the lines above
``ac_low`` Hz (the AC path's coupling). The measurement path has a hidden gain error (ppm) and
offset (V), the instrument's own errors; the ADC's calibration coefficients correct them::

    raw     = true × (1 + gain_error_ppm·1e-6) + offset
    reading = (raw − cal.offset) × cal.gain

With ``ranges`` the meter ranges (metrology-authoring.md 2): the function's full-scale values,
a manual ``range`` (a value the range must be able to measure; the smallest fitting range is
used, as SCPI prescribes) and ``autorange`` (the range follows the true value; above
``autorange_up`` × full scale or below ``autorange_down`` × it, the smallest range that fits
the value is taken). The hidden errors may be one number (every range alike) or per function
and range: ``{DC: {0.1: 8, 1: 3}, AC: 60}``.

params.name: ac_low
params.doc: Hz above which lines count into the AC reading

params.name: function
params.doc: DC | AC: what a command without one measures; what sample() reads

params.name: ranges
params.doc: full-scale value of each range, per function ({DC: [...]}) or one list

params.name: range

params.name: range_res

params.name: range_curr
params.doc: the DCI/ACI functions' own manual range, A (None: `range`, #301)

params.name: autorange
params.doc: the range follows the true value

params.name: autorange_up
params.doc: fraction of full scale above which the range switches up

params.name: autorange_down
params.doc: fraction of full scale below which the range switches down

params.name: gain_error_ppm

params.name: offset
params.doc: the meter's own DC offset error, V (hidden); per function and range

dmm_input_terminal.doc:
The DMM's input terminals (#190 E1): the electrical input and its impedance to ground.

``pin`` is the instrument's electrical terminal (a definition exposes it as ``IN``); ``out``
carries the measured signal on to the conditioning block. With ``z_in`` the terminal models its
own input stage, so the resistance enters the bench circuit: ``z_in_high`` on the
``high_z_ranges`` when ``high_z`` is set. Without ``z_in`` the terminal is a pass-through and
an ``input_port`` in front owns the electrical side.

The high-impedance choice follows the range in use, which the conditioning block knows; the
terminal references it (``conditioning``).

params.name: z_in
params.doc: input resistance the terminal puts on the net itself, ohm (None: the wiring's)

params.name: z_in_high
params.doc: input resistance when high_z applies, ohm

params.name: high_z
params.doc: high input impedance (a setting)

params.name: high_z_ranges
params.doc: the ranges on which high_z applies (full-scale values)

params.name: conditioning
params.doc: the conditioning block whose range decides high_z

params.name: mode
params.doc: What the terminal does (#301): VOLT reads the net; RES/FRES push the range's test current into the DUT and read V/I (FRES: V on the sense terminal, the four-wire pair); CURR puts the range's shunt across the input and reads V/R. The reading comes from the circuit.

params.name: test_current
params.doc: A per resistance range (full-scale ohm -> A), or one number

params.name: shunt
params.doc: ohm per current range (full-scale A -> ohm), or one number

params.name: compliance
params.doc: V the resistance source can reach: above it the reading is an overload

eload_input.doc:
The load's input terminal and switch (#186 C1): the element that stamps the circuit.

It owns the ``in`` port; with the input off (or a protection trip latched) it is an open
circuit. Otherwise it stamps what the mode loop decided: a current sink (CC/CP), a resistance
(CR or the CC knee) or a voltage clamp (CV). ``c_in`` adds the input capacitance to ground.

params.name: enabled
params.doc: the input switch (a setting)

params.name: c_in
params.doc: input capacitance to ground, F

params.name: loop
params.doc: the eload_mode_loop that owns the mode

params.name: protection
params.doc: the eload_protection whose trip opens the input

eload_meter.doc:
The load's V/I/P measurement (#186 C1). The readings keep the ``load.*`` keys the front
panel uses; the input stage supplies the solved values.

params.name: input
params.doc: the eload_input whose solved values are read

params.name: ov_bit
params.doc: STATus:QUEStionable bit positions (#343). questionable bit set while OVP is tripped

params.name: oc_bit
params.doc: questionable bit set while OCP is tripped

params.name: op_bit
params.doc: questionable bit set while OPP is tripped

params.name: unr_bit
params.doc: questionable bit set while the input is on but unregulated

operations.name: questionable
operations.doc:
STATus:QUEStionable:CONDition? (#343): the condition register, live — OV / OC / OP while
that protection is tripped, UNR while the input is unregulated (:meth:`EloadInput.unregulated`).
The bit positions are parameters, so a model maps its own manual's register.

eload_mode_loop.doc:
The static function and the operating-point mode (#186 C1): CC, CV, CR or CP.

``function`` names the static mode; the setpoint belongs to it (``current``, ``voltage``,
``resistance`` or ``power``). ``von`` is the starting voltage: below it a CC (or CP) load does
not sink. ``slew`` (A/µs) limits how fast the CC current follows a setpoint change; the ramp is
evaluated at the current virtual instant, so a later reading sees the intermediate current.

The mode loop is piecewise in the D34 sense: :meth:`update_mode` reads the solved input voltage
and the present sink current and chooses ``("open"|"i"|"r"|"v", value)`` — a current sink, a
resistance or a voltage clamp (CV mode). The CP hysteresis (I = P/V) is iterated to a
self-consistent point; the decision D52 records the semantics and its limit.

params.name: function
params.doc: CC | CV | CR | CP: the static operation mode

params.name: current
params.doc: A, the regulated current in CC

params.name: voltage
params.doc: V, the regulated input voltage in CV

params.name: resistance
params.doc: ohm, the resistance in CR

params.name: power
params.doc: W, the power in CP

params.name: von
params.doc: V, starting voltage: a CC/CP load does not sink below it

params.name: slew
params.doc: A/µs, CC setpoint slew rate (0: instantly)

params.name: stage
params.doc: the eload_power_stage carrying the envelope

eload_power_stage.doc:
The sink's operating envelope (#186 C1): the CC knee, the current and power capability.

In constant current mode the load cannot go below its minimum operating resistance ``r_min``:
below the knee voltage (``r_min`` × the set current) it behaves as that resistance instead of
the current sink. ``i_max`` and ``p_max`` cap every mode (the constant-power envelope), so a
CC setpoint above the capability is power-limited rather than drawn.

params.name: r_min
params.doc: minimum operating resistance in CC mode (the knee), ohm

params.name: i_max
params.doc: maximum sink current, A

params.name: p_max
params.doc: maximum sink power, W (0: no power limit)

eload_protection.doc:
OVP / OCP / OPP protection (#186 C1): thresholds, the trip latch and its kind.

A threshold of 0 disables that protection. When the operating point crosses one the trip is
latched and the input stops conducting (the mode loop opens); :meth:`op_clear` resets it (the
model's protection-clear command; #194 maps the DL3000's own). The thresholds are checked on
the solved operating point, so a trip is a DC behaviour, not a transient one.

params.name: ovp
params.doc: over-voltage trip, V (0: off)

params.name: ocp
params.doc: over-current trip, A (0: off)

params.name: opp
params.doc: over-power trip, W (0: off)

function_generator_core.doc:
Standard waveforms with phase-continuous frequency changes.

Parameters: ``function`` (SINusoid, SQUare, RAMP, DC; Siglent's SINE, SQUARE are the same),
``frequency`` (Hz), ``amplitude`` (Vpp), ``offset`` (V), ``phase`` (degrees), ``duty`` (% high,
square), ``symmetry`` (% rising, ramp; 100 is a sawtooth), ``bandwidth`` (Hz, harmonic limit for
square and ramp), ``square_max`` (Hz, highest square/ramp frequency), ``amplitude_unit`` (what
``amplitude`` means: VPP, VPK or VRMS of the waveform).

params.name: function
params.doc: SINusoid | SQUare | RAMP | DC (SINE, SQUARE are aliases)

params.name: frequency
params.doc: Hz

params.name: amplitude
params.doc: in amplitude_unit

params.name: offset
params.doc: V

params.name: phase
params.doc: degrees

params.name: bandwidth
params.doc: Hz, harmonic limit for square and ramp

params.name: square_max
params.doc: Hz, highest square/ramp frequency (inf: none)

params.name: duty
params.doc: percent high time of the square

params.name: symmetry
params.doc: percent rising half of the ramp (100: sawtooth)

params.name: amplitude_unit
params.doc: VPP | VPK | VRMS: what amplitude means

input_port.doc: An electrical input with a resistive (and optional capacitive) impedance to ground.

params.name: z_in
params.doc: input resistance to ground (FIFTY and ONEMEG are named values)

params.name: c_in
params.doc: input capacitance to ground

lead.label: 测试导线
lead.doc:
A test lead on a wire: a real series resistance (metrology-authoring.md 6).

Unlike a ``series`` accessory such as a cable, it is not negligible: the termination check does
not look through it and the bench circuit solves the drop across it.

params.name: r
params.doc: series resistance

load_resistor.label: 对地电阻
load_resistor.doc: A resistor from its one terminal to the bench ground (a load on a single-ended net).

params.name: r
params.doc: resistance to ground

lockin_aux.doc:
The AUX block (D3 #189): four ADC inputs and four DAC outputs on the bench, circuit level.

Each input is a high-impedance (``z_in`` to ground) ADC terminal; each output is a Thevenin
source of ``dac`` volts behind ``z_out``. The inputs read the solved voltage of their nets, so a
wire to another instrument or a DUT matters exactly as it does for any other circuit block.

params.name: dac1
params.doc: V, DAC output 1

params.name: dac2
params.doc: V, DAC output 2

params.name: dac3
params.doc: V, DAC output 3

params.name: dac4
params.doc: V, DAC output 4

params.name: z_in
params.doc: input resistance to ground, ohm

params.name: z_out
params.doc: series output impedance of a DAC, ohm

operations.name: set_dac
operations.doc:
``AUXV n,v``: set DAC output ``index`` (1..4) to ``voltage`` through the definition's
``aux.output<n>`` state, so the value is a setting of the instrument like any other.

lockin_input_amp.doc:
The low-noise front-end amplifier (D3 #189): the sensitivity full scale, the dynamic reserve,
the absolute input limit and the front-end noise density.

Readings are input-referred (the gain does not scale X, Y or R); sensitivity sets full scale for
the overload limits and the auto-gain ladder, and the reserve widens the limit over it. The
signal itself passes through unchanged, which is what makes the outputs input-referred.

params.name: sensitivity
params.doc: V rms full scale: overload flags and auto gain, not the scaling of X, Y, R

params.name: reserve
params.doc: 20 dB of dynamic reserve over the sensitivity

params.name: reserve_db
params.doc: The reserve as a table of dB by full-scale sensitivity (#273, the SR830's p.4-8 table per RMOD): {sensitivity V: dB}; between entries the dB follow log(sensitivity). Set, it replaces `reserve`.

params.name: input_limit
params.doc: V peak

params.name: noise_density
params.doc: V/√Hz, hidden state

lockin_input_filter.doc:
The input coupling and the line-frequency notches (D3 #189, SR830 block diagram).

AC coupling is a first-order high-pass at ``ac_corner``; the line notch (and its second
harmonic) is a second-order band-stop of quality ``notch_q`` at ``line_frequency``. Both act on
the spectral lines (data level, like the coupling the old monolith applied); the input
impedance, shielding and the differential pair are the circuit part of the input terminal.

params.name: coupling
params.doc: DC | AC input coupling

params.name: ac_corner
params.doc: Hz, corner of the AC coupling high-pass

params.name: line_notch
params.doc: the line-frequency notch on

params.name: notch_2x
params.doc: the notch at twice the line frequency on

params.name: line_frequency
params.doc: Hz the notches sit on

params.name: notch_q
params.doc: quality factor of the notches (a model value)

lockin_input_mode.doc:
The input configuration (#273, the SR830's ISRC): single-ended A, differential A − B, or the
current input.

The terminals are ``input_port`` blocks in front (their impedance is the circuit part: 10 MΩ
for the voltage inputs; the current input is ``current_z`` to a virtual ground, so the
definition binds the A port's ``z_in`` to the same setting). This block forms the signal the
chain measures: A, A − B, or the current into A (its voltage over ``current_z``) times
``current_scale`` V/A, so the voltage sensitivities read as currents scaled by 1/current_scale
(``lockin_output.unit_scale``). Shield grounding is not a circuit element here: bench nets
are referred to one ground, so floating or grounding the shield changes no reading.

params.name: mode
params.doc: A | A-B | I: single-ended, differential, or the current input on A

params.name: current_z
params.doc: ohm, the current input's impedance to its virtual ground

params.name: current_scale
params.doc: V the chain sees per A in the current input (1 µA <-> 1 V)

lockin_lowpass.doc:
The n-pole RC low-pass (D3 #189): time constant, slope (6 dB/oct per pole), the closed-form
settling from a new regime, the equivalent noise bandwidth, and the truncation check that
queues 329 when a truncated input still passes the filter.

params.name: time_constant
params.doc: s, filter time constant T

params.name: slope
params.doc: dB/octave of the low-pass; 6 per pole (24: 4 poles)

params.name: truncation_limit
params.doc: filter gain past which truncated input raises error 329

params.name: mixer
params.doc: the lockin_mixer that multiplies the input by the reference

lockin_mixer.doc:
The phase-sensitive detector (D3 #189): the input's spectral lines multiplied by the
reference, each becoming a complex exponential at Δf = f − f_detect, plus the input's DC term.
The low-pass filter is applied to those exponentials by ``lockin_lowpass``.

lockin_output.doc:
The DC output (D3 #189): X/Y with offset and expansion, R/θ, the overload flags and their
errors, the front-end noise of the reading, auto gain and auto phase — and the sampler the data
buffer reads (X/Y/R/θ at the buffer's instants).

Offset and expansion are display-level: ``offset_x``/``offset_y`` are percent of full scale
(subtracted) and ``expand`` multiplies the deviation from the offset; R and θ always show the
raw outputs. The defaults (0 %, x1) leave X and Y untouched.

params.name: filter
params.doc: the lockin_lowpass (the settling output)

params.name: amp
params.doc: the lockin_input_amp (sensitivity, reserve, noise)

params.name: sample_rate
params.doc: Hz, the data buffer's sampling rate (SRAT)

params.name: offset_x
params.doc: percent of full scale subtracted from X (display level)

params.name: offset_y
params.doc: percent of full scale subtracted from Y

params.name: expand
params.doc: 1 | 10 | 100: the deviation from the offset is multiplied by this

params.name: expand_x
params.doc: Per quantity (#273, the SR830's OEXP): X, Y and R each with their own expand (None: `expand`); R's offset and expand act on the displayed R only, the R output stays raw. X's own expand (None: expand)

params.name: expand_y
params.doc: Y's own expand (None: expand)

params.name: offset_r
params.doc: percent of full scale subtracted from the displayed R

params.name: expand_r
params.doc: the displayed R's expand (None: expand)

params.name: unit_scale
params.doc: The unit of X, Y and R per volt the chain measures (#273): 1 for a voltage input; the current input's 1/current_scale (1e-6: the readings and the sensitivity are in A).

params.name: readings
params.doc: The readings table (#383, the SR86x OUTP?/SNAP? parameter list): entry k is index k, {word: X, source: X}. A source is X, Y, R, THETA, XNOISE or YNOISE (this output), $path (a setting's value) or <component>.<quantity> (that block's trace_value: an AUX input, the reference frequency). Empty: OUTP?/SNAP? by X, Y, R, THETa as before.

operations.name: auto_gain
operations.doc: Smallest 1-2-5 sensitivity that keeps R under 90 % of full scale and the input in range.

operations.name: auto_phase
operations.doc: Move the reference phase so that the settled output has θ = 0.

operations.name: measure_display
operations.doc:
OUTR? i (SR830 manual 5-16): the value display channel i shows — the quantity its DDEF
picks. ``target`` is the definition's ``<component>.<quantity>`` for that setting, the same
sources a ``curve_buffer`` trace reads (X/R/XNoise and AUX1/2 on CH1, Y/θ/YNoise and
AUX3/4 on CH2). ``ratio`` (#390): the quantity the display divides by (DDEF's ratio, an AUX
input; empty: none); a denominator of 0 V shows 0.

operations.name: readout
operations.doc:
``OUTP? j`` / ``SNAP? j,k{,l}`` / ``SNAPD?``: the table's parameters by index or word, all at
one instant, comma separated in the order asked (#383).

lockin_reference.doc:
Internal oscillator or tracking of the fundamental on REF_IN; harmonic n; SINE_OUT drive.

Outputs: ``ref``, a unit line at the detection frequency n·f whose phase is n·ψ + φ (the
demodulator's reference), and ``sine``, the SINE_OUT drive at f (``amplitude`` in V rms) on
the dc ``dc_level``.
An external reference needs at least ``min_vpp`` peak to peak; when it disappears the
oscillator keeps running at the last frequency and error 327 is queued once.

params.name: source
params.doc: INTernal | EXTernal: track the fundamental on REF_IN

params.name: frequency
params.doc: Hz of the internal oscillator

params.name: phase
params.doc: degrees, phase of the detection reference

params.name: harmonic
params.doc: detection at harmonic n x f

params.name: amplitude
params.doc: V rms of the SINE_OUT drive

params.name: dc_level
params.doc: V, the dc level added to the SINE_OUT drive (the SR86x's SOFF, #407)

params.name: min_vpp
params.doc: V peak to peak an external reference needs to lock

params.name: f_max
params.doc: Hz, the highest detection frequency n x f (#273: the SR830's 102 kHz)

params.name: over_limit
params.doc: Past f_max: "refuse" the setting (-221), or "clamp" the harmonic to the largest that fits (the SR830 manual's rule for HARM and FREQ).

params.name: ext_slope
params.doc: What on REF_IN defines zero phase (#273, the SR830's RSLP): SINE the positive-going zero crossing of a sine; RISE a TTL rising edge (on a sine, the same crossing); FALL a TTL falling edge, half a period later (the reference moves by 180°).

mux_card.doc:
A multiplexer card's relays and analog bus (#191 E2, first wave: 34901A, 20 channels).

Every channel is a two-wire input (``H``/``L``); a closed relay connects it to the card's
internal analog bus through the contact resistance ``relay_r``. The bus carries the internal
DMM's input resistance (asked of the ``dmm`` terminal, so a high-impedance range changes it)
and its voltage is the signal the internal DMM measures — closing a channel therefore loads
the DUT on that channel. ``close_limit`` is the number of relays that may be closed at once:
the first wave's card is break-before-make while scanning, so the default is one, and a second
closure is refused (-221).

The relay state lives in the instrument's channel state (``ch<n>.<relay_state>``, declared as
``channel_state`` by the definition); the card reads it whenever it stamps the circuit.

params.name: slot
params.doc: the module slot the card sits in

params.name: relay_r
params.doc: contact resistance of a closed relay, ohm

params.name: relay_settle
params.doc: s from closing a relay to a settled reading (card switching time)

params.name: close_limit
params.doc: relays that may be closed at once (0: no limit)

params.name: relay_state
params.doc: the channel state a relay writes: ch<n>.closed

params.name: backplane
params.doc: the daq_backplane component (slots and modules)

params.name: dmm
params.doc: the internal dmm_input_terminal whose input resistance loads the bus

params.name: four_wire_offset
params.doc: Four-wire pairing (#301): in FRES, channel n carries the test current and channel n + four_wire_offset the sense (34901A: n and n+10, n = 1..10). 0: no four-wire.

params.name: current_channels
params.doc: the module's current channels (34901A: 21, 22; with a shunt)

operations.name: close
operations.doc: ``ROUTe:CLOSe (@101)`` closes the channel; the query replies whether it is closed.

output_control_loop.doc:
The voltage/current control loop and its limit switch (D34), reusable by any output stage.

A definition binds the setpoint (``function``, ``v_level``, ``i_level``), the limits
(``i_limit``, ``v_limit``) and the output setting to it. The piecewise output stage calls
:meth:`update_mode` with the metered terminal voltage and the source current; the loop picks
CV or CC and the sign of a current-limited source, as the SMU's output stage does.

``envelope`` optionally names a component whose ``limit_cap(function, level)`` caps a limit by
the range in use (the SMU's source DAC); a supply that has no such table leaves it empty. A
channel-level loop names its channel's ``power_stage`` in ``channel_envelope`` instead (B2).

params.name: function
params.doc: VOLTage | CURRent: what the terminal is forced to

params.name: v_level
params.doc: V, setpoint in voltage mode

params.name: i_level
params.doc: A, setpoint in current mode

params.name: i_limit
params.doc: A, current limit in voltage mode

params.name: v_limit
params.doc: V, voltage limit in current mode

params.name: output
params.doc: the output stage is enabled

params.name: envelope
params.doc: instrument-level component capping the limits by the range in use

params.name: channel_envelope
params.doc: a channel's power_stage (B2), same interface

output_stage.doc:
A Thevenin source driving an electrical pin from a signal input.

``load_setting`` is the load the instrument assumes when it defines its amplitude (D13): the
source EMF is scaled so that a load of that value would see the requested voltage. ``inf`` means
the amplitude is the open-circuit voltage; so does any setting of ``hiz_from`` ohms or more, for
instruments whose high-impedance setting is a number (a calibrator's ``LOAD 10000``).

params.name: z_out
params.doc: series output impedance, ohm

params.name: enabled
params.doc: False: the pin floats

params.name: load_setting
params.doc: load the amplitude is defined for (D13), ohm; inf: open circuit

params.name: invert
params.doc: invert the polarity of the output

params.name: hiz_from
params.doc: a load_setting of this many ohms or more counts as high-Z, ohm

passive_probe.label: 无源探头
passive_probe.doc:
A divider probe: series resistance from tip (IN) to the scope connector (OUT).

With ``attenuation`` N and ``r_tip`` the total tip resistance into the nominal scope input
``r_scope`` (1 MΩ), the series element is ``r_tip - r_scope`` (9 MΩ for a 10x, 10 MΩ probe).
The division then follows from the scope's actual input impedance, as on a real bench.
Probe capacitance and compensation are not modeled (transients are out of scope, D10).

params.name: attenuation
params.doc: nominal division ratio (10: a 10x probe)

params.name: r_tip
params.doc: total resistance from the tip into the scope input

params.name: r_scope
params.doc: the nominal scope input resistance the series element assumes

params.name: c_pf
params.doc: probe capacitance (not modeled, D10)

power_output.doc:
The output stage (B2 #185): relay, remote sense and the source the loop programs.

The relay closes ``relay_s`` after the output is switched on (and opens at once when it is
switched off), so the output timings count in virtual time (D12). The source is a voltage
source regulating the sense pair (or the force terminals) in CV mode, a current source in CC
mode — the same elements the SMU's output stage uses, driven by the reused control loop.

params.name: output
params.doc: the output switch (a setting)

params.name: remote_sense
params.doc: regulate the sense pair instead of the force terminals

params.name: r_out
params.doc: output impedance of the pass stage, ohm (parallel outputs stay solvable)

params.name: relay_s
params.doc: s from switching the output on to the relay closing

params.name: loop
params.doc: this channel's output_control_loop (the reused B1 loop)

params.name: stage
params.doc: this channel's power_stage (the envelope)

params.name: protection
params.doc: this channel's supply_protection (the trip latch)

params.name: combination
params.doc: the instrument's supply_tracking (an internal pair idles output 3; "" none)

power_stage.doc:
The channel's power stage (B2 #185): voltage/current capability and the current-limit cap.

``limit_cap`` is what the reused ``output_control_loop`` asks its envelope: the current limit a
channel may program. ``v_max`` is the voltage ceiling the output stage clips the programmed
level to, so a definition whose state allows a wider number still cannot over-drive the stage.

params.name: v_max
params.doc: V, the channel's maximum output voltage (magnitude)

params.name: i_max
params.doc: A, the channel's maximum current

params.name: p_max
params.doc: W, the channel's maximum output power

power_supply_setpoint.doc:
A channel's setpoint DAC (B2 #185): the voltage and current levels, within the channel's
range (``stage.v_max`` / ``stage.i_max``). The control loop programs from the same settings.

params.name: voltage
params.doc: V, programmed output voltage

params.name: current
params.doc: A, current limit

params.name: stage
params.doc: the channel's power_stage (range and envelope)

prbs_source.doc:
A pseudo-random bit stream, NRZ at ``rate`` bits/s between ±``level``.

Periodic with 2^n − 1 bits, so its spectrum is lines at k·rate/N: the DFT of the sequence times
the rectangular pulse's sinc. Exact, not estimated by an FFT of samples (D13); lines are kept
for ``lobes`` sinc lobes, within the line limit.

params.name: order
params.doc: LFSR order n: period 2^n - 1 bits (one of 5, 6, 7, 9, 10, 11, 15)

params.name: rate
params.doc: bit rate, bits/s

params.name: level
params.doc: V: the bits swing between +level and -level

params.name: lobes
params.doc: sinc lobes of spectrum kept

rc_lowpass.label: RC 低通
rc_lowpass.doc: Series R from IN to OUT, C from OUT to ground. ``tol_r`` / ``tol_c`` are hidden tolerances.

params.name: r
params.doc: series resistance

params.name: c
params.doc: capacitance to ground

params.name: tol_r
params.doc: relative tolerance of r, hidden (0.1: +10%)

params.name: tol_c
params.doc: relative tolerance of c, hidden

reading_buffer.doc:
Named reading buffers: a DMM's reading memory, an SMU's ``defbuffer1`` and the ones a script
makes. Commands name a buffer with ``name``; without one they use ``default``.

params.name: default
params.doc: the buffer commands use when they name none

params.name: capacity
params.doc: readings a buffer keeps (a made buffer gives its own)

params.name: when_full
params.doc: stop: new readings are dropped | overwrite: the oldest go

params.name: digits
params.doc: readings with a fixed number of digits (None: the definition's format)

params.name: max_buffers
params.doc: buffers there may be, the default one included

params.name: missing_error
params.doc: a buffer name, index or count that does not exist

params.name: empty_error
params.doc: reading from an empty buffer

operations.name: actual
operations.doc: ``TRACe:ACTual?``: readings in the buffer (an SMU's name for ``points``).

operations.name: clear
operations.doc: ``TRACe:CLEar``: empty the buffer.

operations.name: data
operations.doc:
``TRACe:DATA? start,end,"buffer",READ,REL``: readings start to end (from 1), each with the
elements asked for (READ: the reading, REL: seconds since the first, or a sampler field).

operations.name: delete
operations.doc: ``TRACe:DELete "name"``: remove a buffer that was made (the default one stays).

operations.name: make
operations.doc: ``TRACe:MAKE "name",n``: a new buffer of ``n`` readings.

operations.name: points
operations.doc: ``DATA:POINts?``: readings in the buffer.

operations.name: read_clear
operations.doc:
``R? [max]``: the oldest readings (all, or at most ``count``) as an IEEE 488.2 definite-length
block of comma-separated numbers, taken out of the buffer.

operations.name: remove
operations.doc: ``DATA:REMove? n``: the n oldest readings, taken out of the buffer.

reference_clock.doc:
The source's frequency reference: an internal oscillator off by ``ppm`` (hidden; a deviations
entry), or with ``source`` EXTernal the 10 MHz on ``ref`` when one within ±10 ppm is there (the
internal oscillator otherwise, as a real source falls back when it cannot lock).

params.name: source
params.doc: INTernal | EXTernal (a setting such as $clock_source)

params.name: ppm
params.doc: the internal oscillator's frequency error, ppm (hidden)

params.name: nominal_hz
params.doc: the external reference's frequency

resistor.label: 电阻
resistor.doc: Base class for every component type.

params.name: r
params.doc: resistance

rf_attenuator.doc:
The output step attenuator (D2 #188). This model has no attenuation steps — its level is
exact over the whole range (validation-rfgen.md) — so ``attenuation`` is 0 dB unless a
definition sets it.

params.name: attenuation
params.doc: dB of output attenuation

rf_level_control.doc:
The level control and ALC (D2 #188): the level in dBm into a matched 50 Ω load. The model's
level is exact over the whole range (no ALC dynamics, settling or level error,
validation-rfgen.md), so this block is the conversion from dBm to the carrier's EMF.

params.name: level
params.doc: dBm into a matched load (a setting such as $power.level)

params.name: synthesizer
params.doc: the rf_synthesizer whose level sweep sets the level (#291; empty: none)

rf_mod_source.doc:
The internal low-frequency modulation source (D2 #188): the tone of AM, FM or PM at its set
frequency. Its frequency is synthesized from the same timebase as the carrier, so the
reference's error scales it too; FM modulates with a phase shift of −π/2 (a sine tone), PM in
phase with the carrier.

params.name: am_rate
params.doc: Hz of the AM tone

params.name: fm_rate
params.doc: Hz of the FM tone

params.name: pm_rate
params.doc: Hz of the PM tone

params.name: clock
params.doc: the rf_reference (empty: an exact clock)

rf_modulator.doc:
The modulator (D2 #188): AM, and Bessel FM/PM truncated at Carson's rule, applied to the
carrier line. FM and PM are exclusive (the later one wins with -221), AM may be added to
either, pulse modulation is refused (-221), and a modulation index needing more than
``LINE_BUDGET`` lines is refused (-222) on the setting that causes it. ``enabled`` is the
master switch (#290): off, the carrier passes bare and every modulation keeps its settings.

params.name: enabled
params.doc: the master modulation switch (Mod/on, :MODulation:STATe, #290)

params.name: am
params.doc: amplitude modulation on

params.name: am_depth
params.doc: percent modulation depth

params.name: am_rate
params.doc: Hz of the AM tone (the modulator forms the sidebands at it)

params.name: fm
params.doc: frequency modulation on (FM and PM are exclusive)

params.name: fm_dev
params.doc: Hz peak deviation

params.name: fm_rate
params.doc: Hz of the FM tone (β = deviation / rate)

params.name: pm
params.doc: phase modulation on (FM and PM are exclusive)

params.name: pm_dev
params.doc: rad of phase deviation (the modulation index beta)

params.name: pm_rate
params.doc: Hz of the PM tone

params.name: pulm
params.doc: pulse modulation (setting it errors: not simulated)

params.name: source
params.doc: the rf_mod_source (the modulating tone, with the timebase error)

rf_reference.doc:
The 10 MHz timebase (D2 #188): the generic reference clock, plus the REF_OUT output.

``ppm`` is the timebase error: hidden state (D9), readable only by measuring. With ``source``
EXTernal the 10 MHz on ``ref`` locks the generator when one within ±10 ppm is there, and every
synthesized frequency carries that error instead; REF_OUT carries the error of the timebase in
use (10 MHz at +4 dBm into a matched load).

params.name: source
params.doc: INTernal | EXTernal (a setting such as $clock_source)

params.name: ppm
params.doc: the internal oscillator's frequency error, ppm (hidden)

params.name: nominal_hz
params.doc: the external reference's frequency

params.name: ref_out
params.doc: the REF_OUT output on (a setting such as $rosc.output)

params.name: out_level_dbm
params.doc: REF_OUT level into a matched load (a fixed model value)

rf_synthesizer.doc:
The carrier synthesizer (D2 #188): the CW frequency, or the sweep/list plan and its current
point, advanced by ``:INITiate`` and ``:TRIGger``. The line it emits is unit amplitude at the
set frequency times the timebase error of the reference it locks to; level and modulation come
later in the chain.

params.name: frequency
params.doc: Hz of the CW carrier

params.name: mode
params.doc: CW | LIST | otherwise the start/stop sweep

params.name: start
params.doc: Hz, first frequency of the sweep

params.name: stop
params.doc: Hz, last frequency of the sweep

params.name: points
params.doc: points of the sweep

params.name: spacing
params.doc: LINear | LOGarithmic

params.name: manual
params.doc: current sweep point, 1-based

params.name: clock
params.doc: the rf_reference (empty: an exact clock)

params.name: manner
params.doc: What sweeps, as the instrument's sweep-state words (#291): a list such as [FREQuency], [LEVel], [LEVel, FREQuency] or [OFF]; None leaves it to `mode` (frequency only).

params.name: level_start
params.doc: dBm, first level of a level sweep

params.name: level_stop
params.doc: dBm, last level of a level sweep

params.name: step_by
params.doc: How the points advance (#291): TRIGger — one point per :TRIGger (`manual`); TIME — one point per `dwell` of virtual time from the sweep's start (D12).

params.name: dwell
params.doc: s per point when stepping by time

params.name: run
params.doc: SINGle: one pass, then the last point holds; CONTinuous: the pass repeats

operations.name: initiate
operations.doc: Start the sweep again from its first point (and, stepping by time, from now).

operations.name: list_freq
operations.doc: ``:LIST:FREQ 1e9,2.4e9`` or ``"1e9,2.4e9"``: real instruments take both forms (D13).

scan_table.doc:
The scan table (#191 E2): a channel list read as one run, and the sampler behind it.

``list`` is the scan list in SCPI channel numbers (a definition binds it to an ``int_list``
setting, e.g. ``ROUT:SCAN (@101:110)``); ``ascending`` scans it in ascending channel order (the
34970A's rule) instead of the order it was written; ``count`` is how many times the list is
scanned per run and ``interval`` the wait between two scans (stored for the model's timing;
the first wave times each reading with the relay settling time plus the DMM's reading time).
The scan runs
through the trigger model: each of its readings closes its channel (the card's
break-before-make rule), reads the internal DMM and carries the channel number in the ``CHAN``
field, so the reading buffer keeps channel and value together.

params.name: list
params.doc: scan list in SCPI channel numbers

params.name: ascending
params.doc: scan in ascending channel order (the 34970A's rule), not list order

params.name: count
params.doc: scans of the list per run

params.name: interval
params.doc: s between two scans

params.name: mux
params.doc: the mux_card that closes the channels

params.name: dmm
params.doc: the dmm_adc that takes each reading

params.name: backplane
params.doc: the daq_backplane that validates the channel numbers

params.name: channel_settings
params.doc: Per-channel measurement configuration (#365): channel setting -> the instrument setting the internal DMM reads, e.g. {function: sense.function, nplc: sense.nplc}. Before a channel is checked or read, its own values (ch<n>.<key>) are loaded into the DMM's.

params.name: function_setting
params.doc: the channel setting CONFigure? names first (e.g. function)

operations.name: configuration
operations.doc:
``CONFigure? (@101)``: the channel's function, range and resolution as one quoted string,
``"VOLT +1.00000000E+01,+3.00000000E-06"`` (the DMM's CONFigure? for that channel).

scope_acquisition.doc:
Run control, sampling and the records of a scope, built from the scope's modules.

One component for every oscilloscope model, set by parameters (instrument-authoring.md 3.2, 8.4).
It names the modules it reads: ``horizontal`` (a ``scope_timebase``), ``trigger`` (a
``scope_trigger``), ``adc`` (a ``scope_adc``), and per channel ``vertical`` (a
``scope_vertical``: the scale and offset) and ``probe`` (a ``scope_probe``, whose output is wired
to ``in<n>``). Written the earlier way, with the modules' parameters on the acquisition itself and
no module named, the definition is expanded into the modules when it loads (a macro):

* **run control** ``mode`` and the values that mean ``auto``, ``normal``, ``single``, ``stop``
  and ``force`` (one frame whatever the trigger, then stop); ``after_single`` is the mode a
  completed single acquisition leaves (empty: the mode stays and the scope stops).
  ``reacquire`` says when a read gets a new acquisition from a running scope: ``explicit``
  (only a digitize command), ``every_read`` or ``on_read_start`` (a read from the first point;
  later pieces read the same record). A pending single acquisition is retried on every read.
  ``missing: acquire`` reads a channel that has no record yet, ``error`` refuses it;
* **noise** the input noise comes from the channel's ``scope_vertical`` ``noise_table``, per
  division at the input connector, in display volts times the probe ratio; it is keyed by
  ``noise_key``: ``time`` (the absolute sample instants, D46; ``noise_stream`` names a setting
  that selects another stream) or ``acquisition`` (the acquisition count, so pauses of any
  real length between commands give the same numbers); ``trigger_jitter_s``;
  * **processing** (F4, D46) what the quantized codes go through: ``normal`` keeps them;
    ``average`` (``averages``) is the mean of that many acquisitions, each of them noisy and
    quantized, so the noise falls by √N and the resolution gains (it takes N acquisitions'
    time); ``peak`` examines each record interval at the ADC's native rate (at most
    ``peak_max_oversample`` samples per record sample) and keeps, of the interval's smallest
    and largest code, the one that departs farther from its ends — a pulse the record rate
    would step over shows up; ``eres`` smooths ``4**eres_bits`` codes (a boxcar), so the
    noise falls by ``2**eres_bits`` — that many more effective bits, at the boxcar's
    bandwidth.

* **synchronization** (instrument-authoring.md 8.4, G2): ``completion: immediate`` finishes a
  single acquisition, a digitize or a forced frame within the command that starts it;
  ``pending`` makes it an operation that finishes in virtual time, when the record after the
  trigger is full: until then the trigger status is waiting (then triggered), a read gets the
  previous record (``while_waiting: previous``) or an error (``error``), ``*OPC?`` and ``*WAI``
  wait for it unless ``opc_waits`` is false, and a digitize waits for it. Without a trigger it
  waits for one, looking again whenever a command arrives; ``no_trigger: wait`` leaves ``*OPC?``
  unanswered meanwhile (the client times out), ``return`` answers it at once.

Per-channel ``ch<n>.display`` says which channels are acquired. The trigger status
(``status_text``), an acquisition type with its count (``acquire_type``, ``acquire_counts``)
and the read-only figures (op ``figure``: points, sample rate, acquisitions) are declared.
Measurements are a ``scope_measurements`` module, the transfer and its preamble a
``waveform_transfer``.

params.name: horizontal
params.doc: the scope_timebase component

params.name: trigger
params.doc: the scope_trigger component

params.name: adc
params.doc: the scope_adc component

params.name: vertical
params.doc: the per-channel scope_vertical component (its name without ch<n>.)

params.name: probe
params.doc: the per-channel scope_probe component (its name without ch<n>.)

params.name: overhead_s
params.doc: virtual time an acquisition takes besides its record, s

params.name: digitize_stops
params.doc: :DIGitize leaves the scope stopped (the InfiniiVision's rule, #248)

params.name: mode
params.doc: the run mode setting

params.name: auto
params.doc: modes that keep untriggered acquisitions

params.name: normal
params.doc: modes that wait for a trigger

params.name: single
params.doc: modes that acquire once on the next trigger

params.name: stop
params.doc: modes that stop (none: a stop command stops)

params.name: force
params.doc: modes that take one frame whatever the trigger, then stop

params.name: after_single
params.doc: the mode a completed single acquisition sets (empty: unchanged)

params.name: reacquire
params.doc: explicit | every_read | on_read_start

params.name: missing
params.doc: error | acquire

params.name: untriggered
params.doc: the time an untriggered acquisition takes: search | record

params.name: noise_key
params.doc: acquisition | time

params.name: noise_stream
params.doc: a setting that selects another noise stream (time key)

params.name: trigger_jitter_s
params.doc: rms offset of each record around the trigger, s

params.name: processing
params.doc: normal | average | peak | eres: what the quantized codes go through

params.name: averages
params.doc: acquisitions an average is the mean of (processing: average)

params.name: eres_bits
params.doc: effective bits a high-resolution acquisition gains (boxcar of 4^b codes)

params.name: peak_max_oversample
params.doc: native samples a peak-detect interval examines at most

params.name: status_text
params.doc: op status: the trigger status as the model words it (stopped, waiting for a trigger, triggered, running untriggered in an auto mode)

params.name: acquire_type
params.doc: op acquire_type: the acquisition type setting and, per type that takes a count, the setting the count writes, its allowed values and how a query writes it, e.g. {AVERage: {setting: acquire.average, values: [4, 16], format: "{kind},{value:d}"}}

params.name: acquire_counts
params.doc: type -> {setting, values, format} for the types that take a count

params.name: completion
params.doc: immediate | pending: when a single acquisition or digitize is done

params.name: opc_waits
params.doc: *OPC?, *OPC and *WAI wait for a pending acquisition

params.name: while_waiting
params.doc: previous | error: a read while an acquisition is pending

params.name: no_trigger
params.doc: wait | return: *OPC? while armed for a trigger that has not come

operations.name: acquire_type
figure
operations.doc:
A read-only figure of the acquisition: ``points`` (record length), ``sample_rate`` or
``count`` (acquisitions so far, an integer). Numbers come in the definition's number
format, as an integer with ``integer``, or in engineering notation with ``significant``
digits.

operations.name: force_trigger
operations.doc: ``FRTR``: one acquisition now, triggered or not; a single acquisition then stops.

operations.name: opc
operations.doc: ``*OPC?`` answers ``1`` once a pending single acquisition is done; ``*OPC`` sets the ESR bit.

operations.name: run
operations.doc:
``:TRIGger:RUN``: run again; in a single mode, arm one acquisition. A model whose stop is a
mode (LeCroy's STOP) runs in its first auto mode.

operations.name: run_mode
operations.doc:
``:TRIGger:MODE``, ``TRMD``: a single mode arms one acquisition (and acquires at once if
it can), a force mode takes one frame and stops, a stop mode stops.

operations.name: self_cal
operations.doc:
A user self-calibration: every channel re-derives its calibration constants against the
scope's internal references (``scope_vertical.self_calibrate``; a channel without a
calibration store has nothing to write). The reply is the diagnostic code ``0``; the
command's ``reply`` template gives the model's words (e.g. ``*CAL {value}``).

operations.name: single
operations.doc: ``ARM``: one acquisition, like setting the first single mode.

operations.name: wait
operations.doc: ``WAIT [timeout]``: until a pending single acquisition is done (or the timeout passes).

scope_adc.doc:
The ADC group shared by a scope's channels: resolution, top sample rates and interleaving.

``bits`` (0: records are not quantized) and ``codes_per_div`` (0: ``2**bits / divs``) set the
quantization; ``offset_sign`` says whether the offset setting is added to or subtracted from the
volts. ``max_rate`` is the top sample rate (0: no limit); channels of a ``rate_pairs`` pair share
a converter, so with both on the top rate is ``max_rate_paired``.

params.name: bits
params.doc: 0: records are not quantized

params.name: codes_per_div
params.doc: 0: 2**bits / divs

params.name: divs
params.doc: divisions the ADC spans

params.name: offset_sign
params.doc: add | subtract: how the offset setting enters the codes

params.name: max_rate
params.doc: top sample rate, Sa/s (0: no limit)

params.name: max_rate_paired
params.doc: the top rate when both channels of a rate pair are on

params.name: rate_pairs
params.doc: channels sharing a converter, e.g. [[1, 2], [3, 4]]

scope_frontend.doc: The earlier name of ``scope_vertical`` (same behavior), kept so existing definitions load.

params.name: coupling
params.doc: DC | AC | GND

params.name: bandwidth
params.doc: -3 dB point of the first-order low-pass

params.name: bw_limit
params.doc: bandwidth limit on, or a named filter (FULL, 20M)

params.name: bw_limit_hz
params.doc: the limit when bw_limit is on

params.name: ac_corner
params.doc: corner of the AC coupling high-pass

params.name: scale
params.doc: V/div as displayed

params.name: offset
params.doc: V as displayed

params.name: probe_ratio
params.doc: the probe setting the displayed scale and offset include

params.name: scale_range
params.doc: [min, max] V/div at the input connector (None: any); may map a setting

params.name: offset_ranges
params.doc: [[up to V/div, +-limit V], ...] at the input connector (None: any)

params.name: out_of_range
params.doc: error: refuse with -222 | clamp: take the nearest legal value

params.name: noise_table
params.doc: [[V/div, noise V rms], ...] at the input, per division (None: quiet)

params.name: gain_error_ppm
params.doc: this unit's gain error, ppm (hidden); a number or by input V/div

params.name: offset_error
params.doc: this unit's offset error, V at the input (hidden); a number or by V/div

params.name: dac_error_ppm
params.doc: the offset DAC's gain error, ppm of the offset setting (hidden)

params.name: store
params.doc: the calibration_store correcting the record, keyed by the displayed V/div

params.name: record
params.doc: the acquisition component holding the records

params.name: source
params.doc: the channel measured (a setting such as $measure.source); empty: the command's

params.name: names
params.doc: model name -> [engine measurement, unit], e.g. {AMPL: [VAMPlitude, V]}

params.name: top_base
params.doc: histogram | extremes

params.name: levels
params.doc: percent | absolute: what mid is

params.name: mid
params.doc: the crossing level a period is counted on

params.name: hysteresis
params.doc: half the counter's band, of top minus base

params.name: min_cycles
params.doc: complete cycles a period needs

params.name: clipped
params.doc: measure | invalid: a record at the ADC's limits

params.name: gate
params.doc: [from, to] divisions of the record; None: all of it

params.name: invalid_value
params.doc: what an unmeasurable value answers

params.name: status
params.doc: measured, cannot be measured

params.name: sources
params.doc: the two settings DELay?/PHASe? use without sources, e.g. [measure.source, ...]

params.name: trigger_levels
params.doc: channel -> its trigger level setting, for :TRIGger:LEVel:ASETup

params.name: slots
params.doc: The screen's measurement list (#373): a measurement command without '?' installs one; past `slots` the oldest leaves. 0: no list (the query only answers).

params.name: all
params.doc: the measurements :MEASure:ALL? answers, in order (engine names)

operations.name: all
operations.doc:
``:MEASure:ALL?``: the current value of every measurement of ``all`` on one source, in
that order (a snapshot; nothing is installed).

operations.name: at
auto_trigger_levels
operations.doc:
``:TRIGger:LEVel:ASETup``: every displayed channel's trigger level to its waveform's 50 %
(halfway between top and base; 0 V with AC coupling) — the levels of ``trigger_levels``,
channel -> setting (#350).

operations.name: clear_list
operations.doc: ``:MEASure:CLEar``: no measurements on the screen, their statistics gone.

operations.name: measure
operations.doc:
``:MEASure:VPP? [CHANnel1]``: the engine measurement ``what`` (a constant argument of the
command) in the definition's number format; what cannot be measured is NaN's sentinel.
Without '?' (``:MEASure:VPP CHANnel1``) the measurement goes on the screen's list (#373).

operations.name: named
operations.doc:
A measurement by the model's name (``names``): the value, or ``invalid_value`` when it
cannot be measured; the reply template also gets {kind}, {unit} and {status}, e.g.
'{header} {kind},{value} {unit},{status}'.

operations.name: pair
operations.doc:
``DELay? [<source1>][,<source2>]``: the time from source 1's first rising edge to source 2's
first rising edge at their middle levels; ``PHASe?``: that delay over source 1's period, in
degrees (#350). Without sources, :MEASure:SOURce's two (``sources``).

operations.name: results
operations.doc:
``:MEASure:RESults?``: each installed measurement, oldest first, as
``<label>,<current>,<min>,<max>,<mean>,<std dev>,<count>`` — the statistics of every value
taken since the list was cleared (the current one included). Label: ``<name>(<channel>)``.
Nothing installed: an empty reply.

operations.name: statistics
operations.doc:
The statistics of the values taken so far of a measurement: ``count``, ``mean``,
``sdev``, ``min`` or ``max`` (``item``, a constant argument or a parameter).

scope_probe.doc:
The probe setting of one channel: display volts are the volts at the input times ``ratio``.

A display conversion, not part of the analog path (instrument-authoring.md 8.4). ``skew``
(bound to the model's channel-skew setting where it has one) and ``skew_error`` (this unit's
own, a ``deviations`` draw) delay the channel's record by that many seconds: the acquisition
samples the channel's signal that much earlier (instrument-authoring.md 8.4, G3). A real
scope applies the delay after the ADC, so the trigger path — which detects on the analog
signal — is not delayed with it.

params.name: ratio
params.doc: probe attenuation the display assumes (1, 10, ...)

params.name: keywords
params.doc: op set_ratio: what the probe command's keywords mean (a ratio, or "value": the number that follows), the range of a ratio, and the display settings that scale with it

params.name: ratio_range
params.doc: [min, max]; None: any positive ratio

params.name: rescales
params.doc: settings in display units that follow the ratio, e.g. [$ch.scale, $ch.offset]

params.name: skew
params.doc: the channel's skew setting, s (unbound: the model has none)

params.name: skew_error
params.doc: this unit's own skew error, s (hidden; a deviations entry)

operations.name: set_ratio
operations.doc:
``:CHANnel<n>:PROBe VALue,10`` / ``DEFault``: a keyword gives the ratio or says the number
that follows is; the ``rescales`` settings scale with it (the display shows probe-tip
volts). The query answers the ratio in the definition's number format.

scope_timebase.doc:
The horizontal system: time per division, the record length rule and the trigger position.

``record_length``: ``fixed`` (``points`` over ten divisions), ``exact`` (the rate is
``points / 10 div`` up to the ADC group's top rate) or ``rate_ladder`` (that rate rounded down
to a 1-2-5 step; samples ``1 / rate`` apart). The trigger sits at the centre, or ``delay``
seconds before it when that is bound. A model with a reference mode setting places it from
``reference_mode`` (DELay / POSition) and, in POSition mode, from ``reference_position``
percent across the record.

The sampling clock has a frequency error ``clock_ppm`` (this unit's own, a ``deviations``
draw); with ``rosc`` EXTernal it follows the 10 MHz on ``ref`` instead, whose fractional
error the instrument inherits (instrument-authoring.md 8.4, G3). A fast clock takes samples
closer together than the nominal interval, so the records keep the nominal dt the scope
reports and time measurements read low — the spectrum analyzer's reference convention.

params.name: scale
params.doc: seconds per division (ten divisions across)

params.name: delay
params.doc: unbound: the trigger at the centre of the record

params.name: record_length
params.doc: fixed | exact | rate_ladder

params.name: points
params.doc: record points or memory depth (10000, "10k")

params.name: delay_range_divs
params.doc: [min, max] of delay in divisions, e.g. [-5000, 5]; None: any

params.name: reference_divs
params.doc: where the trigger (delay 0) sits, divisions from the left; may map a setting

params.name: reference_mode
params.doc: A model with a reference mode setting (DELay | POSition) places the trigger from it: in POSition mode the trigger sits `reference_position` percent across the record and the delay setting does not move it; in DELay mode it starts at the centre, moved by `delay`. the reference mode setting; empty: the delay alone places the trigger

params.name: reference_position
params.doc: the trigger position setting, 0..100 percent (POSition mode)

params.name: clock_ppm
params.doc: the sampling clock's frequency error, ppm (hidden)

params.name: rosc
params.doc: INTernal | EXTernal: the clock follows the 10 MHz on ref

scope_trigger.doc:
Edge trigger on its own analog path (instrument-authoring.md 8.4, G5).

The trigger looks at the signal before the ADC, through its own ``coupling`` filter (a table
``filters`` of high-pass and low-pass corners per coupling value: AC, low- and high-frequency
reject), a ``reject`` filter alongside it and ``hf_reject`` (filters keyed HF), with its own
``noise_rms``. An edge counts once the signal has been beyond the
``hysteresis_divs`` band on the far side of the level (``reject_hysteresis_divs`` while
``noise_reject`` is on); the instant is interpolated between samples, so a record reports the
trigger to a fraction of a sample. After a trigger, the next is not taken before ``holdoff``
seconds (while ``holdoff_on``).

``source``, ``level`` and ``slope`` select the edge (``rising`` and ``falling`` list the slope
names that take each); a level or slope per channel is bound with the channel number written
``{n}``: ``$ch{n}.trigger_level``. ``external`` sources read the ``ext`` port (wired from an
instrument input); ``line`` sources trigger on the rising zero crossings of the mains
(``line_hz``, phase zero at the session's start). An auto mode looks ``search_windows``
records ahead (its auto timeout); a normal or single acquisition waits up to
``search_horizon_s`` of virtual time for its edge.

params.name: source
params.doc: a channel (C1, CHANnel1), an external or a line source

params.name: level
params.doc: display volts; per channel: $ch{n}.trigger_level

params.name: level_by_source
params.doc: Each source's own level setting, by source word (#248), e.g. {CHANnel1: trigger.level1, EXTernal: trigger.level5}; a source not listed uses `level`.

params.name: slope
params.doc: per channel: $ch{n}.trigger_slope

params.name: rising
params.doc: slope values that take a rising edge

params.name: falling
params.doc: slope values that take a falling edge

params.name: search_windows
params.doc: records an auto mode looks ahead for an edge (its auto timeout)

params.name: search_horizon_s
params.doc: virtual time a normal or single acquisition waits for an edge, s

params.name: max_search_points
params.doc: samples a search may take (a long horizon is searched coarser)

params.name: level_range_divs
params.doc: the level stays within +-this many divisions of the source's screen

params.name: coupling
params.doc: the trigger path's coupling: a key of filters, or DC

params.name: reject
params.doc: a reject filter alongside the coupling (LFReject, HFReject): a key of filters

params.name: hf_reject
params.doc: on: the filters keyed HF as well (a separate high-frequency reject)

params.name: filters
params.doc: coupling or reject -> [[highpass | lowpass, corner Hz], ...], e.g. {AC: [[highpass, 8]]}

params.name: hysteresis_divs
params.doc: half the band an edge must cross, in divisions of the source

params.name: noise_reject
params.doc: on: the wider band below

params.name: reject_hysteresis_divs
params.doc: the band while noise_reject is on

scope_vertical.doc:
The vertical channel: coupling, bandwidth, and the scale and offset with their ranges.

Analog first-order filters (physics, D13): AC coupling is a ``ac_corner`` high-pass and the
bandwidth a first-order low-pass at ``bandwidth`` (or ``bw_limit_hz`` when the limit is on).
The ``scale`` (V/div) and ``offset`` (V) are display values; with ``scale_range`` and
``offset_ranges`` a change outside the range is refused with -222 and the old value kept. The
ranges are given at the input connector, i.e. the display values divided by ``probe_ratio``
(instrument-authoring.md 8.4). The input noise is a ``noise_table`` row of the scale: real
scopes' noise rides the vertical setting (the front-end gain sets it at the ADC), so a fixed
input value would leave the coarse divisions far quieter than 1 LSB and averaging could not
resolve more (F4, D46).

The unit's own metrology (instrument-authoring.md 8.4, G3). Each V/div at the input
connector has its own attenuator and gain stage: ``gain_error_ppm`` (relative) and
``offset_error`` (V at the input) are what this unit adds there — a number, or one per input
V/div, the table a ``deviations`` entry with ``by: {scale: …}`` draws; a scale the table does
not list has no characterized error and contributes 0. ``dac_error_ppm`` is the offset DAC's
gain error, referred to the displayed offset setting: a display offset of V moves the record
by V·(1 + d), i.e. the reading is off by V·d. The vertical runs before the probe (which is a
display conversion), so the errors ride the input path and the DAC term is divided by
``probe_ratio`` here. They sit in signal order — coupling, the attenuator's gain, the bias,
then the bandwidth — and the record shows them, since it is reconstructed with the nominal
scale and offset. ``store`` names a ``calibration_store`` whose coefficients correct the
record digitally, (raw − offset) × gain, keyed by the displayed V/div
(metrology-authoring.md 4); :meth:`self_calibrate` writes them for every tabulated scale.

The V/I meter (#184 B1): range resistors, A/D, NPLC and the reading memory handoff.

Readings go through a ``trigger_model`` (the ``sampler`` protocol, metrology-authoring.md 3.4):
one reading takes its NPLC time plus the source delay; a sweep's points are the readings of one
run, each point's level driving the terminal while the run lasts. The measure side ranges like
the meter core (#87): ``measure_ranges`` (per function: the voltage and current readings), the
manual ``measure_range_voltage`` / ``measure_range_current``, ``measure_autorange`` with the
same hysteresis, and a reading beyond ``overrange`` × full scale reads ``overload_value``.

The bench front panel reads this component's values (``core.voltage`` …), so the SMU
definitions keep naming it ``core``.

smu_output.doc:
The output stage (#184 B1): HI/LO, remote sense, floating LO and the output relay.

The voltage loop regulates the metered points: ``V(sense_hi) − V(sense_lo)`` with remote sense
on, otherwise the force terminals (``V(hi) − V(lo)``; with ``floating: false`` the LO is bonded
to the bench ground, the model's original behaviour). The current always flows through the
force terminals. A sense terminal left unconnected while remote sense is on makes the reading
operations raise an error (the loop falls back to the force terminals); the bench validator
warns about such a bench (metrology-authoring.md 6).

Not a ``driver`` for bench checks: at its limit it sinks current, so a supply on the same net
is a valid bench (quadrant 2). The control loop it drives holds the mode (D34).

quantity's limit gets on each range, the 21 V / 105 mA boundary by default), and the sweep
(linear, logarithmic or list) that drives a run's levels. The control loop asks it to cap a
limit for the level in use (:meth:`limit_cap`), so the envelope follows a sweep point too.

The combination of outputs 2 and 3 (B2 #185, #259): track, parallel or series.

``mode`` is the instrument's combination state (OFF / TRAC / PAR / SER). Enabling a combination
requires both outputs off (the manual's constraint). ``topology`` says how the model combines:

- ``split`` (E36311A, ±25 V): output 3 is the negative supply. A change of either programmed
  voltage is mirrored to the other — track keeps ``CH3 = −|CH2|``, parallel ``CH3 = CH2`` and
  series ``CH3 = −CH2``; the physical connection is the bench wiring.
- ``internal`` (E36312A / E36313A, two +25 V outputs, user's guide "Specifying the Operation
  Mode" and "Using the Tracking Operation"): track sets output 3 to the same voltage as
  output 2 and vice versa; series and parallel are made inside the instrument — output 2
  delivers the combination (twice the voltage, or twice the current) and output 3 no longer
  operates, so programming it is refused with error 720 (the manual's "CH3 is not allowed
  when serial/parallel/track is enabled"; tracking keeps output 3 programmable, the guide's
  "and vice versa"). Output 2's range follows (its voltage/current settings' limits and the
  ``v_max``/``i_max``/``p_max`` of its stage); leaving the combination brings the
  independent range back and clips a level above it.
